subject: Workload forecast: GPU pool recommendations and slab pricing clarification
messages:

Date: 2027-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Workload forecast: GPU pool recommendations and slab pricing clarification

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Attached is the preliminary template we discussed — I filled in the high-level monthly request/embedding/generation numbers you shared. A couple of clarifying asks so we can put together a fitted Dedicated proposal: 

- Do the monthly numbers in the spreadsheet reflect peak month or average month? If peak, can you give an expected 99th-percentile QPS for inference traffic?
- What is your 95th-percentile context length for the two main models (assist chat model and summarization model)?
- Do you need strict per-request latency SLO (e.g., p95 < 150ms) or is a p95 < 400ms acceptable for non-interactive batch jobs?

Goal: we want to recommend a GPU pool mix (number of A100/RTX equivalents, model-mix pinning, and a slab pricing recommendation) that matches throughput guarantees without overcommitting.

I've attached the workload template. If you can return the filled workbook by EOD Thursday I can loop in our capacity team.

Best,
Dylan

Hi Dylan,

Thanks — I uploaded the filled workbook (monthly actuals + a 12-month forecast) to the Drive link you sent. Summary highlights:

- Current average monthly gen tokens: ~45M; peak month (seasonal) up to 80M.
- Average QPS during peak windows: ~28 qps sustained for 2 hours; 95th percentile single-request concurrency spikes to ~75 concurrent requests across the cluster.
- Context length: assist chat 1,024 tokens (95th pct 1,500); summarization jobs average 3,000 tokens (batch, not latency sensitive).
- Latency: for customer-facing chat we need p95 < 250ms; background summarization can be p95 < 1.2s.

Procurement note: LuminaHealth prefers a 12-month committed slab with a simple stepped discount schedule tied to committed GPU hours. We want visibility on how committed throughput maps to the slab tiers.

Let us know if you need more granularity, happy to hop on a short follow-up call.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of Product Operations, LuminaHealth

Folks,

Forwarding Lumina's filled forecast. Key constraints: p95 chat latency target 250ms, peak sustained ~28 qps, spikes to 75 concurrent, summarization jobs long-context batch work (3k tokens) but latency tolerant. Procurement wants a 12-month slab/commit schedule.

Can you propose:
- a recommended GPU pool composition (count and type) and model-mix allocation,
- committed throughput mapped to slab tiers (e.g., commit X GPU-hours => Y discount), and
- a suggested safety buffer / burst policy (credits or burst pool)

Please respond with a short recommendation and draft pricing grid — I need to include this in our proposal to Lumina by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-11T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: LuminaHealth workload + slab ask — please advise GPU pool recs

Quick sizing note — baseline assumptions from the workbook: chat model = 7 tokens/request avg for generation (interactive), summarization = long context ~3k tokens with batching. I ran a two-scenario estimate: conservative and optimized.

1) Conservative (target p95 < 250ms, minimal prefetch/caching):
- Recommend: 8 x A100-40GB-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) with 2 reserved for summarization batch workers to avoid interference.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~30 qps for chat at p95 target, headroom for 75 concurrent spikes via burst credits.
- Commit: 12-month reserved slab = 65% utilization target on pool => commit 8 * 24 * 30 days * 0.65 = ~3,744 GPU-hours/month.
- Pricing slab suggestion: Tier 1 commit (>=2,000 GPU-hrs/mo) = standard, Tier 2 (>=3,500 GPU-hrs/mo) = 12% discount, Tier 3 (>=5,000 GPU-hrs/mo) = 18% discount and enterprise SLA.

2) Optimized (use prefix caching + lightweight quantized variants for chat):
- Recommend: 6 x A100-equivalent + 2 x RTX-class for low-latency burst. Pin chat model to optimized quantized variant on 4 A100s, keep 2 A100s for mid-weight inference, 2 RTX for cheap burst and batch.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~40 qps with caching; p95 ~180-220ms for chat.
- Commit: target 65% pool utilization => commit ~2,880 GPU-hrs/mo.
- Pricing slab: propose a blended discount: 10% at 2,500+, 16% at 4,000+.

Safety/burst policy: suggest 500 GPU-hour burst credit bucket per month (billed at discounted overage rate) and an automated fallback routing to hosted variant if pool exhausted. Also include one month of free burst credits as a ramp incentive.

Attachments: I exported a short one-pager with the math and two pricing grids (redwood_gpu_pool_recs_v1.pdf). Please review and flag anything I missed.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_gpu_pool_recs_v1.pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Workload forecast: GPU pool recommendations and slab pricing clarification

Hi Maria — thanks for the details and the patience while our capacity team validated numbers. Attaching the one-pager and a proposed 12-month slab grid. Summary recommendation below: 

- Recommended option (balanced): 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs + 2 x RTX-class burst nodes. Commit target: 2,880 GPU-hrs/month (12-month commitment).
- Expected delivered guarantees: p95 chat latency <= 220ms with prefix caching + model-mix optimization; sustained peak window coverage at 28 qps; automated burst credits to handle 75-concurrency spikes.
- Pricing / discounts: 10% discount at commit >=2,500 GPU-hrs/mo, 16% discount at >=4,000 GPU-hrs/mo. We also offer 500 GPU-hr/month burst bucket (first month free) and visibility dashboards for token-level cost and latency.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether Lumina wants the balanced option (recommended above) or the conservative option (8 A100s).
2) If balanced option is OK, procurement preference is noted for a stepped slab — I'll draft the contract term sheet and ship it for review.

If helpful, happy to do a 30-minute call with Karthik/Marissa to walk through the one-pager.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
